gap: No result ChatGPT got works out the cost per promised year of security updates. For the 11.1-inch Lenovo Yoga Tab Gen 2 it is $729.99 ÷ 7 years ≈ $104 per year (launch price; security updates through 2033). For the Galaxy Tab S11 at Samsung US's price today it is $999.99 ÷ 7 ≈ $143 per year. ChatGPT priced the S11 at $899.99 and also recommended the older Yoga Tab, not the Gen 2.
standout_why: I compared against three cited rivals. Tech Advisor (723363) gives the S11 at $799.99 with 7 years of updates and doesn't list any Lenovo Yoga Tab, so its stale price would give $114 per year and miss today's $999.99. iTechGuides gives the A11+ at $299.99/$379.99 and states the 7-year promise for the S11 series, but gives no S11 base price and no per-year cost. Neither covers the Yoga Tab Gen 2 (launched September 2026). I couldn't open Wired (wired.com blocked the fetch). Its Android list is dated 2026-08-13, before the Gen 2 launched, so it can't include it. I didn't open Tom's Guide (2026-11-04) or Android Central, so one of them may mention the Gen 2.
decides: This confirms the S11 for the best screen and S Pen, but at $999.99 at Samsung US today, not the $899.99 ChatGPT showed, it costs about $143 per promised year of security updates. It challenges the 'best value' slot. ChatGPT's $599.99 Best Buy Yoga Tab is the 2025 Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 model, and I couldn't open a Lenovo page giving that model's update promise. The 11.1-inch Yoga Tab Gen 2 has a 7-year promise in Lenovo's launch coverage, at about $104 per year. So the value pick should be the Gen 2, or the older Yoga Tab with a clear warning about its shorter support.
